notes: Identity verified from canonical text: title Monitoring the ebb and flow of attention: Does controlling the onset of stimuli during encoding enhance memory?; Trisha N. Patel, Mark Steyvers, Aaron S. Benjamin; DOI 10.3758/s13421-019-00899-4; Memory & Cognition (2019) 47:706–718. Full primary research report with four experiments, Discussion and References, rather than an abstract or preregistration. No PDF was supplied; embedded forest-plot graphic labels cannot be inspected from canonical text. Original side is an unassigned placeholder and was not investigated. Item-level description and page 10 Discussion identify the item analysis across the four experiments, not the Experiment 4 subject-level test. The printed d is retained without conversion; the authors do not name a further standardisation convention. N is null because this passage/figure caption does not explicitly state the final analytic item-observation count, treatment of repeated items across experiments or exclusions for the pooled item analysis. t(639) is retained only as a test statistic, never used to derive N. Reported success is uninformative because authors explicitly say the item effect alone is difficult to interpret as a benefit, despite its significant p value.
